meta.artefact: The outcome-overlay registry — every success/failure value set that has been run, how it was compiled, and which experiment consumed it
meta.why: The overlay values are a declared-knowledge layer, and the S1 ruling changed them: a lifecycle-distance dependency now grades a transition by how far it travels, not only by its direction. Experiment 1 ran on the pre-distance values, so overwriting them in place would have made a published result unreproducible from the repo. Instead each value set is a named version, exactly as a controller mapping is: a version is selected at the experiment seam, and no layer below there prefers one.
meta.compiled_not_authored: Neither version is hand-authored. Both are compiled from the single rule set at ../outcome_rules.json by mtdsim.l3_simulation.controller.rules, and the 'spec' field below is the whole recipe. `python -m mtdsim.l3_simulation.controller.rules --check` re-compiles every registered version and reports any cell that differs from what is committed — the reproduction check that distinguishes rule-generated values from fitted ones.

schema.name: the version name a caller selects
schema.dir: the directory holding this version's success.json and failure.json
schema.spec: the compilation recipe: relationship_source ('bands' | 'consensus_stages'), whether the distance term applies, the kernel parameters when it does, and success_passthrough (true: the success table compiles to the identity and only the failure table conditions — the failure-only overlay, v4)
schema.consumed_by: the experiments that have run on this version
schema.produced: what it produced, in one sentence
schema.immutable: true once an experiment has consumed it, so a published result stays reproducible

default_rationale: The default is the experiment-1 value, so an unqualified load reproduces what has always run. It is deliberately NOT the newest version: promoting a version to default would re-bake an experiment's choice into the pipeline, which is the coupling this registry exists to remove. Experiments select their version explicitly — the same ruling the controller mapping registry carries. Note that the go-forward version is now v4_failure_only (Marc's 2026-08-19 ruling), not v3 — an experiment must name it explicitly; every record published before 2026-08-19 is keyed on v3.

versions.name: v1_band_relationship
versions.construction: the R2 rule set with the relationship term read from the declared five-band kill-chain prior (0 prep, 1 intrusion, 2 consolidate, 3 expand, 4 objective) and no distance dependency: a pair's value is its first-matching rule's value, full stop
versions.rationale: the values as finalised at R2 after four adversarial cross-examination rounds, certified 82% on internal coherence. Retained unchanged because experiment 1 ran on them.
versions.produced: ASR 0.00 across all 100 movement runs in two profile-determined failure modes (friction and churn). The supervisor's S1 objection is against this version: because relationship is graded by direction only, reconnaissance -> impact carried mass comparable to reconnaissance -> initial-access.
versions.immutability_note: Frozen so experiment 1 stays reproducible. Regenerable from outcome_rules.json under this version's spec, and the reproduction check pins it.

versions.name: v2_lifecycle_distance
versions.construction: the same rule set, with both ordering-dependent terms moved onto the four-stage APT-lifecycle consensus: the relationship is the sign of the consensus stage offset, and the value is multiplied by the declared distance kernel (geometric decay per stage crossed, separate forward and backward ratios, a zero floor). Nothing is hand-edited and no rule value changed.
versions.rationale: executes the S1 ruling. The relationship term stops resting on a declared five-band prior and starts resting on the consensus of five published lifecycle models; the distance term makes a transition's likelihood fall with how far across the campaign it travels, so the long jumps the supervisor named collapse to exactly zero while adjacent steps are untouched.
versions.produced: 40 of 210 pairs change relationship class, all inside the consensus's weakly-ordered post-intrusion middle; 6 pairs per verdict fall to exactly zero (preparation-stage sources to objective-stage destinations). Swept over the declared bands across 2600 runs on both controller mappings, the verdict is mixed: ASR stays 0.00 everywhere and MTD-invariance holds at every point, while the intermediate profile's failure-mode classification and any ordering of profiles by progress do move. The floor z turned out behaviourally inert — no profile net carries a three-stage transition for it to act on, which also means the pair that motivated S1 (reconnaissance -> impact) was a defect in the declared table that never routed mass.
versions.immutability_note: Frozen 2026-07-28: two studies have consumed it, so its values must stay reproducible. Superseded as the go-forward version by v3_persistent_backward, which differs only in delta_ratio.

versions.name: v3_persistent_backward
versions.construction: identical to v2_lifecycle_distance except delta_ratio, the backward decay per extra stage crossed, which moves 0.5 -> 0.25. Same rule set, same relationship ordering, same forward kernel, same floor. Nothing hand-edited.
versions.rationale: Marc's persistence ruling (2026-07-28). Under v2 a full-campaign collapse after a failure — exfiltration falling back to reconnaissance — sat at 0.0625: 14x below a one-step fallback, but not impossible. The ruling is that an attacker persistent enough to reach exfiltration does not abandon its foothold to re-scan the perimeter, so that jump should read as exactly 0, as the three-stage forward leap already does.
consumed_by: experiment 2 — expo02_ashen_lynx (data/results/expo02_ashen_lynx; docs/implementation/pipeline/ogasp/experiment_02_findings.md) and every published movement-arm study since 2026-07-29 (axis-4 structural probe, FSM alignment/succession, disruption frontier, learning readiness, progress credit, predictability, plural preference, …)
the failure-only overlay feasibility study, as the conditioned arm (docs/implementation/pipeline/ogasp/success_null_overlay_feasibility.md)
versions.produced: experiment 2's headline: ASR degenerate at 200 s, breadth suppression per mechanism, the mechanism x profile interaction, and the verdict-blind control indistinguishable from the conditioned arm (axis 4 DESIGNED). The 2026-08-19 feasibility study priced its success table by ablation: a profile-signed 1-3 host effect through the enables tier's coupling to the mapping, no headline moved.
versions.immutability_note: Frozen 2026-08-19: experiment 2 and the studies after it consumed it, so its values must stay reproducible. Superseded as the go-forward version by v4_failure_only on Marc's 2026-08-19 ruling.

versions.name: v4_failure_only
versions.construction: identical to v3_persistent_backward on the failure side — same nine failure rules, same consensus relationship ordering, same kernel (gamma 0.25, delta_ratio 0.25, z 0.1) — and the success table compiled as the constant 1.0 (rule id 'passthrough'), the multiplicative identity, so a success verdict routes on the base flow proportions unchanged. The five success rules stay in outcome_rules.json for v1-v3's reproducibility and are not consulted. Nothing hand-edited.
versions.rationale: Marc's failure-only ruling (2026-08-19). The base flow proportions are taken from reports of campaigns that worked, so base(a->b) already answers 'given success at a, where next' — a success matrix re-weights that measured answer with declared values for the same question, which is a second, weaker-tier encoding of a thing the base already encodes and overrules the evidence wherever it differs. The failure matrix has the opposite status: no corpus records what an attacker did after a step failed, so declared knowledge is the only source. One declared object, encoding the one thing no corpus can. The M2 ruling still holds — the success treatment is the identity (the corpus), the failure treatment is the matrix. Feasibility, the static and behavioural pricing of the dropped column, and the evidence-tier inversion weighed: docs/implementation/pipeline/ogasp/success_null_overlay_feasibility.md.
versions.produced: not yet run as a published configuration. As the in-memory success_null arm of the feasibility study (same values): against v3, a profile-signed effect on breadth of one to three hosts (objective_none_c2 up — its whole v3 deficit was the success table's — objective_exfiltration_impact down), via the enables tier's coupling to the mapping's precondition chain; no experiment-2 headline moved; the failure column alone reacts (more actions, fewer retraces) without changing breadth.
versions.immutability_note: Becomes immutable once a published run consumes it.
